title: CHD2 source-specific interaction, donor, ontology and primary-evidence records
artifact_type: Manual reproducible extraction and explicitly labeled scientific paraphrases, not a provider report or publication cache.

8.text: BioGRID interaction 1438345 records human CHD2 as bait and human TRIM41 as prey in a yeast two-hybrid experiment attributed to PMID:21516116. No exact-pair mammalian validation or tested isoform is asserted.
8.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

9.text: Three positive IntAct records match human CHD2 O14647 and BEND7 Q8N7W2-2 in the 2014 array, pooling and validated two-hybrid stages; partner sufficient-binding-region feature 10-374 is retained.
9.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

10.text: Three positive IntAct records match human CHD2 O14647 and TRIM41 Q8WV44 in the 2014 two-hybrid study; the array record carries partner sufficient-binding-region 86-630.
10.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

11.text: Three positive IntAct records match human CHD2 O14647 and TEKT1 Q969V4 in the 2014 two-hybrid study; neither a native ciliary encounter nor CHD2 structural-cilium activity follows.
11.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

12.text: Three exact positive IntAct records match human CHD2 O14647 and THAP1 Q9NVV9 in the 2014 two-hybrid study. The independently verified partner is a sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription regulator; this supports the binding-class term without establishing a native transcriptional mechanism.
12.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

13.text: Three positive IntAct records match human CHD2 O14647 and MID2 Q9UJV3-2 in the 2014 two-hybrid study; the array record carries partner sufficient-binding-region 21-705.
13.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

7.text: The authentic Baltz primary thesis Table S1 lists CHD2 in class II with L1 -3.46, H1 NA, L2 -3.18, normalized mean +3.32 and iBAQ 5.38. L1 and L2 are light-crosslinked conditions, so the raw H/L signs correspond to enrichment in both measured captures. The table is gene-level and does not identify a CHD2 RNA target or a unique protein isoform.
7.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

6.text: The Castello original paper and extended Methods describe UV-crosslinked HeLa poly(A)-RNA capture with denaturing purification and mass spectrometry. The exact CHD2 supplementary-table entry was not independently recovered. Its preserved human HDA assertion is corroborated by the separate positive Baltz CHD2 capture; no target-specific Castello ratio or validation is invented.
6.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

19.text: Official Reactome event R-HSA-9943412 locates its CHD1/CHD2 set in nucleoplasm. It models binding to H3K4me3-containing nucleosomes, with a mixed CHD1/CHD2 literature summary; it is not an independent direct CHD2 compartment assay.
19.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

23.text: PMID:27783602 Table S1 row 28 identifies linc2025 promoter deletion and a 0.47 increase in neighboring Chd2 expression. Note S5 page 8 treats Chd2 as a transcript readout and leaves the cis mechanism unresolved; it does not test CHD2 protein function. Independent CHD2 protein studies support broad gene-expression involvement.
23.kind: Reviewer paraphrase of the authentic source records or inspected experiments; not a primary-paper quotation.

definition.text: A membrane-bounded organelle of eukaryotic cells in which chromosomes are housed and replicated. In most cells, the nucleus contains all of the cell's chromosomes except the organellar chromosomes, and is the site of RNA synthesis and processing. In some species, or in specialized cell types, RNA metabolism or DNA replication may be absent.
That part of the nuclear content other than the chromosomes or the nucleolus.
Binding to chromatin, the network of fibers of DNA, protein, and sometimes RNA, that make up the chromosomes of the eukaryotic nucleus during interphase.
Any molecular function by which a gene product interacts selectively and non-covalently with DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).
Binding to ATP, adenosine 5'-triphosphate, a universally important coenzyme and enzyme regulator.

An activity, driven by ATP hydrolysis, that modulates the contacts between histones and DNA, resulting in a change in chromosome architecture within the nucleosomal array, leading to chromatin remodeling.

Binding to a histone, any of a group of water-soluble proteins found in association with the DNA of eukaryotic or archaeal chromosomes. They are involved in the condensation and coiling of chromosomes during cell division and have also been implicated in gene regulation and DNA replication. They may be chemically modified (methylated, acetlyated and others) to regulate gene transcription.

Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + H2O = ADP + H+ phosphate. ATP hydrolysis is used in some reactions as an energy source, for example to catalyze a reaction or drive transport against a concentration gradient.

A dynamic process of chromatin reorganization resulting in changes to chromatin structure. These changes allow DNA metabolic processes such as transcriptional regulation, DNA recombination, DNA repair, and DNA replication.
Binding to an RNA molecule or a portion thereof.

summation.text: CHD1 and CHD2 bind to H3K4me3 nucleosomes associated with transcriptionally active regions, although CHD2 binds with significantly lower affinity than CHD1 (Sims et al, 2005; Sims et al, 2007; Flanagan et al, 2005; Flanagan et al, 2007). H3K4me3 binding appears to be mediated at least in part by the N-terminal chromodomains of the proteins (Sims et al, 2005; Sims et al, 2007; Flanagan et al, 2005; Flanagan et al, 2007; Morettini et al, 2011; Kelley et al, 1999). Whether H3K4me3 binding is sufficient for recruitment of CHD to promoters in vivo is not clear; recruitment may instead be mediated by interaction with the RNA polymerase II transcriptional machinery (Siggens et al, 2015). CHD1 and CHD2 have also been associated with transcriptional elongational and splicing factors (Simic et al, 2003; Smolle et al, 2012; Sims et al, 2007; Lee et al, 2017). Studies in Drosophila, yeast, and humans have suggested that CHD1 interacts with Mediator and other chromatin modifying complexes such as FACT (a heterodimer of SSRP1 and SUPT16H in humans), the SAGA and PAF complexes (Kelley et al, 1999; Pray-Grant et al, 2005, Dey et al, 2011).
